        Page drafted with an AI coding assistant; see the disclosure.

        Knowledge Graphs playground

        Write RDF, turn it into a graph and ask it questions with SPARQL. Everything runs in this page: nothing to install, nothing sent to a server, and it works offline.

        Create KG

        Write triples in Turtle or JSON-LD. The text is checked as you type and its triples are listed next to it.

        • Combine your data with the course's recipe graph.
        • Keep the result in memory as a .rete file, query it or download it.

        Validate KG

        Write SHACL shapes and check a graph against them. The report follows your typing: which node breaks which rule, and why.

        • Start from the shapes of the course.
        • Try them on data that is broken on purpose.
        • Validate the graph you created.

        Query KG

        Write SPARQL against a graph in memory. There is no Run button: the answer follows your typing, and a query that does not parse is reported with its line.

        • Start from the worksheet queries in the sidebar.
        • Read the answer as a table, as cards or on a map.
        • Open any .rete file by URL or from disk.

        The engine: rete

        rete (Latin for “net”) stores a whole RDF graph in one immutable .rete file: the term dictionary, the sorted triple indexes and a dataset card. Put the file on any static host and clients run SPARQL against it where it sits, the idea of Parquet or PMTiles applied to RDF graphs.

        This page embeds the rete engine, version , compiled to WebAssembly, together with the recipe graph of the course (). rete is experimental: the file format can change before version 1.0, so a .rete file must be read by the version that wrote it.
